title: Tool Symphony Coordinator: failure islands, loop dampening and structured-result contracts
creator: Samira Khan
description:
Problem: multi-tool chains in the API (function calling + external tool adapters) occasionally create accidental cycles and noisy retries when a tool invokes another agent that can call back into the chain. This causes token waste, broken structured outputs, and spikes in latency.

Goal: implement a lightweight coordinator component that sits in the execution loop to: 1) detect and dampen emergent loops, 2) isolate failure islands so one misbehaving tool doesn't cascade, 3) preserve rich provenance on injected tool results so structured-output contracts can be validated and patched, and 4) provide a compatibility shim for older tool adapters that don't emit the new handshake tokens.

Scope: runtime-level coordinator + compatibility shim + unit/integration tests and observability hooks. Not in scope: full migration of all third-party adapters (we will provide a bridge).

Design notes: the coordinator will assign a short-lived handover token to each tool invocation. Tokens carry depth, causal-path, and a lightweight signature (provenance-salt) used for deterministic replay and structured-result verification. When the coordinator sees a token re-enter the same logical chain beyond a configurable depth threshold, it will: 1) apply an exponential dampening policy (increase probability of short-circuiting the call), 2) optionally rewrite the downstream tool call to a read-only or cached variant, and 3) emit a telemetry event tagged "loop-dampened".

Failure islands: if a downstream tool starts returning non-conformant structured outputs or high error rates (>10% over 1m), the coordinator will isolate the tool into a failure island: future calls in the same chain are routed to a fallback variant (cached/pareto-approx) for a cooling window. This prevents cascade retries and preserves tail-latency SLOs.

Compatibility shim: older adapters will be wrapped with an adapter layer that injects handover tokens and responds to short-circuit directives from the coordinator. The shim exposes a minimal contract: acceptToken(token), onShortCircuit(reason) -> fallbackPayload. Adapters that are upgraded will no longer need the shim and can opt out via a capability flag.

Structured-result contracts: coordinator will validate tool outputs against declared schemas (JSON Schema or Redwood structured-output spec). If validation fails but the payload is repairable (missing optional fields, truncated streaming chunk), the coordinator will attempt a deterministic patch pass using the provenance-salt and cached prefixes before marking the tool as non-conformant. Streaming partials: partial streamed tool outputs will include a stream-seq and last-valid-checkpoint to allow the coordinator to reconcile mid-stream patches without breaking client streaming semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator exposes handover-token header in internal runtime calls and records causal-path in telemetry
Loop detection triggers dampening after configurable depth (default depth=3) and emits loop-dampened events
Failure island isolation routes degraded tool calls to fallback variant for the configured cooling window
Compatibility shim successfully wraps at least two legacy adapters (http-tool and db-tool) and passes integration tests
Structured-result validation rejects non-conformant payloads, and deterministic patch pass repairs >60% of repairable failures in test harness
End-to-end test: synthetic chain that would previously loop now halts/dampens with <5% additional token cost vs baseline
Observability: Grafana dashboard panel shows per-chain loop events, failure-island counts, and patch success rate
comments: 2026-02-18 Samira Khan: Initial ticket created after incident on 2026-02-16 where a three-tool chain caused token blowup (see postmortem link in attachments). Proposing coordinator + shim approach to avoid invasive adapter changes.

2026-02-22 Riley Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype token envelope and basic depth counting. Observed correct detection on synthetic loops. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4598

2026-02-27 Design review (Diego Morales): agreed that exponential dampening is preferred to hard abort; soft-fallbacks maintain UX for streaming clients. Suggested adding a per-customer policy so enterprise tenants can tune sensitivity.
2026-03-03 PM feedback (Asha Patel): emphasize compatibility shim rollout plan and communication to integrations team. Need migration playbook: shim -> opt-out -> native capability.

2026-03-05 Riley Chen: Added structured-output validator module and patcher that uses provenance-salt + cached prefix to repair truncated JSON in stream experiments. Repair rate currently 64% on fuzz tests.

2026-03-08 QA (Riley Chen): Integration tests added for http-tool shim and jdbc-tool shim. One flaky test remains around partial stream reconciliation; investigating sequence gaps when multiple concurrent patches occur.

2026-03-11 Security review kickoff: requested threat model for token mechanics; we will ensure tokens are short-lived, non-guessable, and not persisted in plaintext. Link to review doc in attachments.

2026-03-12 Samira Khan: Planning rollout: feature-flag gated in runtime-2.3. Canary to 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor loop-dampened and failure-island alerts, then 25% for 72h, then full. Post-rollout checklist created.
